name: Multiple Scattering via Spatial Spreading and Ray Marching
definition: A practical technique for rendering multiple scattering effects in volumetric media by avoiding direct numerical simulation of multiple scattering. It uses spatial spreading via a point spread function (PSF) derived from path integral analysis to blur incident illumination, capturing qualitative features like spatial blurring and shadowing more efficiently than Monte Carlo methods.
summary: Multiple Scattering via Spatial Spreading and Ray Marching renders volumetric media by approximating light spreading with a path integral-derived point spread function, offering faster qualitative results than Monte Carlo methods at the cost of higher memory usage.
